classification.difficultyReason: Sketch familiar parent curves and use their increasing shape to turn the given left-to-right order of the inputs into a comparison of output heights.

content.prompt: Suppose $a$ and $b$ are numbers such that $a>b$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: By drawing a graph of $y=e^x$, explain why $e^a>e^b$.

answer.worked: On $y=e^x$, the point with input $a$ lies to the right of the point with input $b$. The curve rises from left to right, so its height at $a$ is greater. Therefore $e^a>e^b$.

spec.description: Increasing exponential with guides from two illustrative inputs to their corresponding output heights.
spec.mathematics: On y = e^x, a is right of b and e^a is above e^b. The x-axis is the horizontal asymptote and (0,1) is the y-intercept.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If $b>0$, draw a graph of $y=\ln(x)$ and explain why $\ln(a)>\ln(b)$.

answer.worked: Both $a$ and $b$ lie in the domain $x>0$. The point with input $a$ is to the right of the point with input $b$. The logarithmic curve rises from left to right, so its height at $a$ is greater and $\ln(a)>\ln(b)$.

spec.description: Increasing logarithm with guides from two illustrative positive inputs to their corresponding output heights.
spec.mathematics: On y = ln(x), a is right of b and ln(a) is above ln(b). The curve crosses at (1,0) and approaches x = 0 from the right.
